admin.secretHint: Write-only: the server keeps it and never shows it again.
admin.reauth.title: Confirm it's you
admin.reauth.body: Every change here asks again, even though you're signed in. Type the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or use a passkey.
admin.reauth.wrong: That code didn't match. Wait for the next one and try again.
admin.reauth.bodyCode: Every change here asks again, even though you're signed in. Type the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
admin.reauth.bodyPasskey: Every change here asks again, even though you're signed in. Your browser asks for your passkey or security key.
admin.reauth.none: Your account has no authenticator app, passkey or security key this browser can use. Add a passkey in Account security, then try again.
admin.reauth.passkeyCancelledOnly: The passkey or security key was not used. Press the button below to try again.
admin.reauth.passkeyUnavailableOnly: This browser can not use a passkey here. Use a browser that can, or add an authenticator app in Account security.
admin.attention.overdue: {count, plural, one {# request is} other {# requests are}} past its due date
admin.attention.requests: {count, plural, one {# privacy request is} other {# privacy requests are}} open
admin.attention.mail: No email server is set up, so invitations have to be passed on by hand
admin.stat.items: {count, plural, one {# live item} other {# live items}}
admin.settings.hint.signups_allowed: When off, people join only by an invitation or through SSO.
admin.settings.hint.signups_verify: Sends a link to the new address. The account can't sign in until the link is opened.
admin.settings.hint.invitations_allowed: Admins can invite people from Users & spaces, even while sign-up is off.
admin.settings.hint.push_enabled: Bitwarden's apps learn of a change through Bitwarden's push relay, so they sync at once and not on a timer. The relay sees that a server has something to say, never what it is.
admin.settings.hint.kemlock_push_relay: Kemlock's mobile apps learn of a change through Kemlock's push relay, so they sync at once and not on a timer. The relay sees that a server has something to say, never what it is.
admin.users.deviceNote: Two-step shows whether the account has a confirmed method. The server holds no more about how people sign in.
admin.users.owner.hint: The new owner has to be a confirmed member of the space.
admin.users.spaces.nameNote: A space's name is sealed under its own key, which the server doesn't have, so spaces are listed by their id.
admin.invites.title: Invitations
admin.invites.sentOf: Sent {count, plural, one {# time} other {# times}}, expires {when}
admin.invites.notMailed: The server couldn't send the email. Pass this link on yourself: it is shown only now.
admin.sso.clearSecretHint: For a provider that treats the server as a public client. Ignored when you type a new secret.
admin.sso.verifiedDomain: Only accept people whose email domain is verified here
admin.sso.verifiedDomainHint: A domain is verified with a DNS record, below. Nobody else can sign in through SSO.
admin.sso.domainsHint: Claim a domain, publish the TXT record at it, then check it. Deleting a claim doesn't sign anyone out.
admin.sso.afterBody: The master password, or a trusted device the person approved on their own.
admin.migrate.from: Vaultwarden data folder on this server, or a mysql:// or postgres:// URL
admin.migrate.files: Data folder beside the database (for MySQL or PostgreSQL)
admin.migrate.filesHint: Holds the attachments, the Sends and rsa_key.pem. Leave it empty when the first field is the data folder.
admin.migrate.readOnly: Nothing was copied. The server only reads and plans for now: kemlock-cli import-vaultwarden is the tool that copies.
admin.events.truncated: The export stopped at 100,000 rows. Narrow the filters to get the rest.
admin.settings.env: Set by {name}, so it can't be changed here.
admin.settings.error.host: Type a host name or address, without https:// or a slash.
admin.settings.domainsHint: Separate domains with commas, such as example.co, example.dev.
admin.settings.error.number: Type a whole number from {min} to {max}.
admin.settings.error.tooLong: That is longer than the server keeps.
admin.settings.key.signups_verify: Verify the email of a new account
admin.settings.key.signups_domains_white: Only these email domains may make an account
admin.settings.key.trash_days: Days in the trash before deletion (Bitwarden-API items; Kemlock apps empty their own trash)
admin.settings.key.event_log_days: Days to keep the event log
admin.settings.key.sign_in_log_days: Days to keep the sign-in log
admin.settings.key.email_log_days: Days to keep the email log
admin.settings.key.deleted_account_grace: Days before an erased account is gone
admin.settings.key.rate_sign_in_per_minu: Sign-in tries a minute, per address
admin.settings.key.rate_password_failure: Wrong passwords in 15 minutes, per account
admin.settings.key.rate_second_step_fail: Wrong two-step codes in 15 minutes, per account
admin.attention.unavailable: The admin API didn't answer, so this list isn't available.
admin.attention.invited: {count, plural, one {# invitation is} other {# invitations are}} still waiting
admin.attention.rsaOnly: {count, plural, one {# account has} other {# accounts have}} only an RSA key, from Vaultwarden
admin.attention.disabled: {count, plural, one {# account is} other {# accounts are}} disabled
admin.attention.peerOffline: {count, plural, one {# paired server is} other {# paired servers are}} offline
admin.attention.keyMismatch: {count, plural, one {# paired server offered} other {# paired servers offered}} a key that doesn't match
admin.users.heading: Users
admin.users.invite.label: Email to invite
admin.users.erase.title: Erase {who}?
admin.users.erase.body: This removes the account's items, files, Sends, devices and tokens, and strips the person's name and email from the event log. It can't be undone.
admin.users.vaultwardenNote: An account moved from Vaultwarden gets its post-quantum key pair the next time one of its Kemlock apps signs in.
admin.users.owner.title: Change owner
admin.events.action.deviceApproved: Approved a sign-in for a new device
admin.events.action.adminBlocked: Failed admin sign-ins, blocked for a while
admin.events.action.mismatch: Refused a federation key that didn't match
admin.sso.lede: SSO decides who may sign in. It never holds or hands out vault keys.
admin.sso.name: Name people see
admin.sso.issuerHint: Works with Keycloak, Authentik, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, Zitadel and any other OpenID Connect provider.
admin.sso.identifierHint: Typed by people whose email domain isn't listed below. Lower-case letters, digits and dashes.
admin.sso.redirect: Redirect URI to register with the provider
admin.sso.pkceHint: Recommended. Needed by providers that treat the server as a public client.
admin.sso.verified: Only accept emails the provider has verified
admin.sso.verifiedHint: An ID token without email_verified: true is refused.
admin.sso.link: Link an existing account with the same email
admin.sso.linkHint: The person still opens their vault with their own key; linking only lets SSO sign them in.
admin.sso.create: Create an account at first SSO sign-in
admin.sso.createHint: Their devices make the keys. The server is told only the public halves.
admin.sso.logout: Sign people out when their provider session ends
admin.sso.logoutHint: Uses back-channel logout. Open vaults lock on the next sync.
admin.sso.test.ok: Last test {at}: discovery found, ID token signed with {alg}, claims present: {claims}.
admin.sso.error.identifier: Use lower-case letters, digits and dashes.
admin.sso.mapHint: Read from the groups claim at each sign-in. A new member still waits for an admin to confirm their key.
admin.sso.after: After SSO, open the vault with
admin.sso.after.trusted: A trusted device, or the master password
admin.sso.after.trustedHint: An approval from one of the person's own devices, or a browser they trusted before.
admin.sso.after.passwordHint: SSO signs in, the password opens.
admin.sso.noKeyConnector: Not offered: a key server that keeps users' keys, as Bitwarden's Key Connector does. Admin approval comes only with a space's account recovery policy, and the member is told.
admin.settings.mail.title: Email
admin.settings.push.title: Push & live sync
admin.settings.push.kemlockHint: Sent by this server: to iPhones with your APNs key, to Android through UnifiedPush; the hosted relay is an optional fallback. A push says only "sync now", never what changed.
admin.settings.push.websocketHint: For the web vault, desktop apps and browser extensions.
admin.settings.twoStep.title: Two-step login methods
admin.settings.twoStep.passkeys: Passkeys and security keys are always on.
admin.settings.storage.title: Storage
admin.settings.storage.databaseHint: PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite. Set at start-up; shown here only.
admin.settings.backups.title: Backups
admin.settings.backups.hint: A backup holds what the server holds: ciphertext. It still needs your users' own keys to open.
admin.settings.join.title: Who can make an account
admin.settings.join.invite: People who are invited, or sign in with SSO
admin.settings.join.domains: Anyone with an email at these domains
admin.settings.join.domainHint: Separate them with commas or spaces, such as example.co, example.dev.
admin.settings.compat.title: Bitwarden compatibility
admin.settings.compat.hint: On, the server serves /api, /identity and /notifications, so Bitwarden apps and Amethystora Vault sync. Off, those routes return 404 and every account is Kemlock only.
admin.settings.error.yubikeyId: A client ID is a number from Yubico.
admin.settings.error.duoHost: A Duo hostname looks like api-xxxxxxxx.duosecurity.com.
admin.settings.error.domains: Type at least one domain, such as example.co.
admin.migrate.lede: Reads a Vaultwarden server's data, plans what a move to Kemlock Server does, and copies it in the background. Nothing is decrypted: items, keys and attachments stay as their owners' apps wrote them.
admin.migrate.path: Vaultwarden data folder, on this server
admin.migrate.error.source: Use at most 1024 characters, with no line breaks or control characters.
admin.migrate.pathHint: The folder with db.sqlite3, attachments, sends, rsa_key.pem and config.json.
admin.migrate.arrives.users: Unchanged. Same master passwords, keys and key derivation settings.
admin.migrate.arrives.organizations: Spaces, with their collections, groups and policies
admin.migrate.arrives.items: Still end-to-end encrypted, as their owners' apps wrote them
admin.migrate.arrives.attachments: Copied to file storage, still encrypted
admin.migrate.arrives.sends: Links keep working while the address stays the same
admin.migrate.arrives.twoStep: Authenticator, passkey, YubiKey OTP, Duo and email setups
admin.migrate.arrives.emergency: With their wait times and any requests open
admin.migrate.arrives.devices: Stay signed in: rsa_key.pem moves too, so their tokens still verify
admin.migrate.arrives.kemlockSync: Each person's Kemlock app moves its items into full sync at its next sign-in, still encrypted
admin.migrate.arrives.amethystora: Unchanged, so Amethystora keeps syncing them
admin.migrate.config.carried: {carried} of {total} carried over. These need you:
admin.migrate.config.push: Kept outside the file. Enter it again under Push.
admin.migrate.config.sso: Not in the file. Enter it in Sign-in & SSO.
admin.migrate.how.twiceHint: Copy everything while Vaultwarden runs, then pause it for a minute and copy what changed.
admin.migrate.how.onceHint: Simplest. Nobody can sync until the address is switched.
admin.migrate.switchBody: Point {host} at Kemlock Server in your reverse proxy. Apps notice nothing.
admin.migrate.switchBack: To go back, point it at Vaultwarden again. Its data is as you left it, though changes made here since won't be in it.
admin.migrate.keepBody: Kemlock apps still sync with any Vaultwarden server, so people who stay on one, or use another, carry on as before.
admin.fed.lede: Servers that copy chosen vaults to each other, as ciphertext. Each keeps its own database, its own sign-in records and its own local vaults. This server is {name}.
admin.fed.offlineBody: Item changes keep syncing through this server. Member, role, policy and key changes wait for the home of each vault.
admin.fed.peersHint: Each server's identity key is pinned when you pair. Traffic between them is sealed twice: TLS outside, and inside it a post-quantum session between the two pinned keys. Event logs go from one server to another only when the sender has Send on and the receiver has Pull on. Both start off.
admin.fed.logs.both: Both ways, paused while it's offline
admin.fed.logs.sendsNotPulled: It sends, but Pull is off here
admin.fed.mismatch.of: Possible man in the middle with {name}
admin.fed.vaultsHint: Every vault is Local, and never leaves this server, until an admin federates it. A federated vault's home orders its members, keys and policy; its replicas follow in order, and a server holds a replica only once its admin accepts.
admin.fed.space: Space · {members, plural, one {# member} other {# members}}
admin.fed.waiting: {n, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}} waiting
admin.fed.demotion.accept.of: Hand over the home of {name} to {peer}
admin.fed.promote.of: Promote to home: this server for {name}
admin.fed.promote.title: Make {self} the home of {vault}?
admin.fed.promote.takes: {self} starts taking its member, role, policy and key changes. {waiting}
admin.fed.promote.nothingWaiting: Nothing is waiting for it now.
admin.fed.promote.epoch: Its home epoch goes from {from} to {to}. That fences {old}: it can't order changes with the old epoch, and when it's back it becomes replica 1 and catches up.
admin.fed.promote.apps: Kemlock apps learn the new server list on their next sync. You can make the old home the home again later.
admin.fed.promote.down: {old} is down, not only cut off from this server
admin.fed.promote.downHint: If it still answers some apps, they keep writing to the old home until it hears about the new one.
admin.fed.consistencyHint: Each pair of servers compares a hash tree of the vaults they share every hour, and again when a peer comes back.
admin.fed.neverBody: Send links, admin settings, the server key, rsa_key.pem and local vaults. The event log, with its sign-ins and IP addresses, goes to a peer only when you send it and that peer pulls it.
admin.fed.neverNote: Each server keeps its own sign-in records; apps sign in to a replica with their device key.
admin.pair.title: Pair a server
admin.pair.lede: Two paired Kemlock Servers copy the vaults you choose to each other, as ciphertext. This server is {name}.
admin.pair.ledeBare: Two paired Kemlock Servers copy the vaults you choose to each other, as ciphertext.
admin.pair.giveCode: Give the other admin this code
admin.pair.codeExpires: Works once. Expires at {at}, in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
admin.pair.enterCode: Enter the code the other server shows
admin.pair.error.address: Type the web address of the other server, starting with https:// or http://, such as https://peer.example.org.
admin.pair.error.code: Type the code as the other server shows it, like 7KP2-WQ4N-D8RJ.
admin.pair.connected: Connected to {name} at {address} with its code. Compare the keys before you go on.
admin.pair.compareBody: The {peer} console shows these same six words. Read them out with its admin, on a call or side by side. Once paired, each server pins the other's key. If a key ever changes, copying stops until you pair again.
admin.pair.words: The six words for both keys
admin.pair.match: The six words match what the {peer} console shows
admin.pair.matchHint: If they don't, cancel: someone may be between the two servers.
admin.pair.confirmEach: {operator} runs {name}, not you. Confirm each of these before you pair.
admin.pair.ack.metadata: {name} sees the metadata of the vaults it holds
admin.pair.ack.metadataHint: It can't open any vault, but it sees how big each one is, when it changes and who its members are.
admin.pair.ack.noDelete: You can't make {name} delete what it holds
admin.pair.ack.noDeleteHint: If you stop sharing a vault or unpair later, the copies {name} already has are up to its operator.
admin.pair.ack.border: Copying a vault to {name} is a cross-border transfer
admin.pair.ack.borderHint: {name} is in {there} and this server is in {here}.
admin.pair.shareBody: Vaults whose home is this server. You can change each one later on the Federation page. {peer}'s admin still accepts each vault before it holds a copy.
admin.pair.shareNone: No vault has its home here, so there is nothing to offer yet.
admin.pair.sendHint: {peer} gets them only if its admin turns on Pull for this server.
admin.pair.pullHint: You get {peer}'s logs only if its admin turns on Send for this server.
admin.pair.logsHint: Both start off. You can change them later on the Federation page.
admin.pair.paired: Paired with {name}. Its identity key is pinned.
admin.peer.ledeSelf: Pick a server on the Federation page to see its keys. This server's own keys are below.
admin.peer.revokeBody: Stops copying with this server and forgets its pinned key. You then pair again with a new one-time code.
admin.peer.layersBody: TLS outside, and inside it a post-quantum session between the two servers' own keys. A proxy that ends TLS sees only sealed frames.
admin.peer.signed: Each change signed where it was accepted
admin.peer.pinnedBody: {date}, when you paired. Both admins compared the six words.
admin.peer.canChangeBody: A rotation signed by this key, or pairing again with a new code. Nothing else is accepted.
admin.peer.suitesBody: The server that connects takes the first suite in the other's list that it supports. There is nothing weaker to fall back to.
admin.peer.suitesCaption: Suites in {name}'s order, beside this server's order
admin.peer.event.refused: Refused an unknown server at the first message
admin.peer.event.mismatch: {name} offered an identity key that doesn't match
admin.peer.ownBody: {name}'s own signed descriptor, at /fed/v1/descriptor and /.well-known/kemlock-federation. Peers read it before every handshake.
admin.peer.kemRotated: New key exchange key made and signed. Sessions already open keep theirs until they rekey.
admin.peer.holding: Where its private keys are held
admin.peer.holding.tpmHint: The keys can't be copied off this machine; if it's lost, peers see a new key and you pair again.
admin.peer.holding.sealedHint: For machines without a TPM. A backup of the database and the server key restores them.
admin.peer.rotate1: Makes a new identity key and signs it with the current one.
admin.peer.rotate2: Every peer checks that signature and pins the new key. Nobody pairs again, and the six words change.
admin.peer.rotate3: Open sessions end and start again with the new key.
admin.peer.acceptOrder: Suites this server accepts, most preferred first
admin.peer.acceptOrderHint: A peer that connects here takes the first one in this list that it supports.
admin.peer.suite.aes: ML-KEM-1024 + X25519 key exchange, AES-256-GCM frames
admin.peer.suite.chacha: ML-KEM-1024 + X25519 key exchange, ChaCha20-Poly1305 frames. Faster without AES instructions.
admin.peer.suite.fips: ML-KEM-1024 + P-384, signed with ML-DSA-65 + ECDSA P-384. Off until a FIPS peer pairs.
admin.peer.order.none: No suite is on, so no peer could connect. Turn at least one back on.
admin.peer.order.aesFirst: This server has AES instructions, so AES-256-GCM is first.
admin.peer.order.chacha: ChaCha20-Poly1305 is first, which suits a server without AES instructions.
admin.peer.order.chachaSlower: This server has AES instructions, so AES-256-GCM would be faster here than ChaCha20-Poly1305.
admin.peer.order.fips: The FIPS suite is first, so any peer that has it on uses P-384 in place of X25519.
admin.peer.order.other: The first suite is the one a connecting peer tries first.
admin.peer.saveHint: Saving signs this server's descriptor again with the new order.
admin.mismatch.title: Possible man in the middle
admin.mismatch.lede: A server answering as {name} offered an identity key that isn't the one you pinned when you paired on {date}. This server refused the session and accepted nothing from it. Copying with {name} stays paused until you choose what to do.
admin.mismatch.keys: The pinned key and the one offered
admin.mismatch.pinnedOn: Pinned {date}, after both admins compared the six words
admin.mismatch.notSigned: Not signed by the pinned key.
admin.mismatch.neverSeen: Never seen on this server before.
admin.mismatch.doesNotMatch: The two keys do not match.
admin.mismatch.whenBody: {at}. It tried {more, plural, =0 {no more times} one {# more time} other {# more times}}, the last at {last}.
admin.mismatch.tlsValid: Passed, with a valid certificate for {cert}. The mismatch is inside, in the session between the two servers' own keys.
admin.mismatch.tlsInvalid: Failed: the certificate was not valid for this server's name.
admin.mismatch.refusedAtBody: The first handshake message. No frame was read and no change was stored.
admin.mismatch.loggedBody: {n, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} in the event log
admin.mismatch.pausedBody: Paused for this server only. Nothing else stops.
admin.mismatch.pausedChanges: {members, plural, one {# member change} other {# member changes}} and {keys, plural, one {# key change} other {# key changes}} wait.
admin.mismatch.stillWorkingBody: Members keep syncing items with this server from their devices. {local, plural, one {# local vault isn't} other {# local vaults aren't}} affected.
admin.mismatch.details: Details for the other server's admin
admin.mismatch.copied: Copied. Send it over a channel you already trust, such as a call or a chat you've used before, not to an address in this alert.
admin.mismatch.keepHint: The default. {name} stays refused, each new try is refused and logged, and this alert stays until the key is sorted out.
admin.mismatch.kept: Still blocking. Nothing changes until you pair again or a signed rotation arrives.
admin.mismatch.pairAgain: Pair again with a new code
admin.mismatch.pairAgainHint: Once their admin confirms they reinstalled or replaced the key. You'll confirm it's you first, then compare the new six words together.
admin.mismatch.confirmItBody: Pairing again replaces the pinned key, so this server asks for a fresh check, even though you're signed in.
admin.mismatch.rotationWhy: Not available: the offered key isn't signed by the pinned key, so this isn't a rotation. A signed rotation is accepted on its own and never raises this alert.
admin.mismatch.mean1: Someone is between the two servers
admin.mismatch.mean1Hint: Traffic for {name} reached another machine. It can end TLS, but it can't show the pinned key.
admin.mismatch.mean2Hint: A fresh install makes a new identity key. Restoring the server key or the TPM with the database keeps the old one.
admin.mismatch.mean3: Its admin replaced the key without signing the change
admin.mismatch.mean3Hint: A new key signed by the old one would have been accepted without asking you.
admin.mismatch.meanFoot: If someone is in between, {name}'s console shows this alert too. Ask its admin on a call or another channel you already trust.
admin.peer.fetchFailed: The descriptor could not be read again ({reason}). The last copy read is shown.
admin.peer.noDescriptor: No descriptor of this peer has been read yet.
admin.mismatch.pausedWaiting: {n, plural, one {# change waits} other {# changes wait}} to be exchanged ({size} held here).
admin.migrate.runningHint: This page follows the move. You can leave it: the server keeps going.
admin.settings.key.security_contact: Who to tell about a problem with this server (an email address, or a mailto:, tel: or https: address)
admin.settings.key.security_encryption: Where their PGP key is (an https: address)
admin.reauth.passkeyOrKey: Use a passkey or security key
admin.reauth.passkeyCancelled: The passkey was not used. Try again, or type a code instead.
admin.reauth.passkeyUnavailable: This browser can not use a passkey here. Type a code instead.
admin.push.title: Push
admin.push.lede: Kemlock's mobile apps learn of a change through a push that says only "sync now", never what changed. This server sends it itself: nothing passes through anyone else.
admin.push.apple.off: Not set up: add your APNs key (see the self-hosting docs)
admin.push.relay.title: Hosted relay (optional)
admin.push.relay.lede: Only a fallback for iPhones on a server without an Apple key. It is off unless you turn it on, and it sees only a device's push token and that something changed.
admin.push.installation: This server's id at the relay
admin.push.onBody: This server is registered with the relay. iPhones it has no Apple key for are pushed to through it.
admin.push.offBody: This server is not registered with the relay.
admin.push.disable.title: Turn the hosted relay off?
admin.push.disable.body: This erases this server's installation at the relay and here. iPhones with no Apple key on this server go back to syncing on a timer until you turn it on again.
admin.push.unavailable: This server has no push relay to turn on or off.
admin.settings.key.kemlock_push_relay_ur: Another Kemlock push relay (an https: address; empty for Kemlock's)
admin.settings.key.backup_schedule: Schedule (off, nightly at 03:00 UTC, or every 6 hours)
admin.settings.key.backup_destination: Folder inside the data folder (empty for backups)
admin.settings.address.title: Address and data folder
admin.settings.address.differs: The address chosen at setup is not the one in use. Apps and passkeys use the address in use; to move, change DOMAIN in the server's configuration and restart it.
admin.settings.address.note: These two stay in the server's configuration and can't be changed here: sign-in proofs are checked against the address, and the data folder holds the database and the server's key. Change them in the environment or kemlock.toml and restart.
